passages.text: About that time, King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church.
passages.sermon:
King Herod was the ruler at that time.
He acted against some people from the church.
He tried to harm them.
These people belonged to the Christian community.
passages.original: Κατ’ ἐκεῖνον δὲ τὸν καιρὸν ἐπέβαλεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ βασιλεὺς τὰς χεῖρας κακῶσαί τινας τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας

passages.text: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.
passages.sermon:
King Herod acted against the church.
He killed James.
James was the brother of John.
Herod killed James with the sword.
passages.original: ἀνεῖλεν δὲ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰωάννου μαχαίρῃ

passages.text: And seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod proceeded to seize Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
passages.sermon:
King Herod ruled at that time.
He saw that harming the church pleased the Jews.
He had already killed James, the brother of John.
Herod decided to arrest Peter also.
This happened during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
passages.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὅτι ἀρεστόν ἐστιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον ἦσαν δὲ αἱ ἡμέραι τῶν ἀζύμων

passages.text: He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the ruler.
Herod arrested Peter.
Herod put Peter in prison.
Herod gave Peter to four squads of soldiers.
Each squad had four soldiers.
The soldiers guarded Peter.
Herod planned to bring Peter out to the people after the Passover.
passages.original: ὃν καὶ πιάσας ἔθετο εἰς φυλακήν παραδοὺς τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις στρατιωτῶν φυλάσσειν αὐτόν βουλόμενος μετὰ τὸ πάσχα ἀναγαγεῖν αὐτὸν τῷ λαῷ

passages.text: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was fervently praying to God for him.
passages.sermon:
Herod put Peter in prison.
Peter stayed in prison.
The church prayed for Peter.
The church prayed to God.
The church prayed with great intensity.
passages.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν Πέτρος ἐτηρεῖτο ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ προσευχὴ δὲ ἦν ἐκτενῶς γινομένη ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν περὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: On the night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with sentries standing guard at the entrance to the prison.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the ruler.
Herod planned to bring Peter to trial.
It was the night before the trial.
Peter was in prison.
Peter was sleeping.
Two soldiers were beside Peter.
Peter was bound with two chains.
Sentries stood guard at the entrance to the prison.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἤμελλεν προαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἡρῴδης τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ ἦν ὁ Πέτρος κοιμώμενος μεταξὺ δύο στρατιωτῶν δεδεμένος ἁλύσεσιν δυσίν φύλακές τε πρὸ τῆς θύρας ἐτήρουν τὴν φυλακήν

passages.text: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.
passages.sermon:
An angel from the Lord appeared suddenly.
A bright light shone in the cell.
The angel tapped Peter on his side.
The angel woke Peter up.
The angel said, “Get up quickly.”
The chains fell off Peter’s wrists.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἐπέστη καὶ φῶς ἔλαμψεν ἐν τῷ οἰκήματι πατάξας δὲ τὴν πλευρὰν τοῦ Πέτρου ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων Ἀνάστα ἐν τάχει καὶ ἐξέπεσαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἁλύσεις ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν

passages.text: “Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”
passages.sermon:
An angel from the Lord spoke to Peter.
The angel said, "Get dressed."
The angel said, "Put on your sandals."
Peter obeyed the angel.
The angel said to Peter, "Wrap your cloak around you."
The angel said, "Follow me."
passages.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς αὐτόν Ζῶσαι καὶ ὑπόδησαι τὰ σανδάλιά σου ἐποίησεν δὲ οὕτως καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Περιβαλοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου καὶ ἀκολούθει μοι

passages.text: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus.
Peter left the cell.
Peter followed the angel.
Peter did not know the angel’s actions were real.
Peter thought he was seeing a vision.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἠκολούθει καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τὸ γινόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἐδόκει δὲ ὅραμα βλέπειν

passages.text: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.
passages.sermon:
Peter and the angel walked together.
They passed the first guard.
They passed the second guard.
They reached the iron gate.
This gate led into the city.
The iron gate opened for them by itself.
Peter and the angel went outside.
They walked down one street.
Suddenly, the angel left Peter.
passages.original: διελθόντες δὲ πρώτην φυλακὴν καὶ δευτέραν ἦλθαν ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην τὴν σιδηρᾶν τὴν φέρουσαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἥτις αὐτομάτη ἠνοίγη αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐξελθόντες προῆλθον ῥύμην μίαν καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέστη ὁ ἄγγελος ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a follower of Jesus.
Peter had just escaped from prison with the help of an angel.
Peter realized what had happened.
Peter said, "Now I know the truth."
Peter said, "The Lord sent His angel."
Peter said, "The Lord rescued me from Herod's power."
Peter said, "The Lord saved me from all that the Jewish people expected to happen."
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος εἶπεν Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Κύριος τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατό με ἐκ χειρὸς Ἡρῴδου καὶ πάσης τῆς προσδοκίας τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.
passages.sermon:
Peter realized what had happened.
Peter went to the house of Mary.
Mary was the mother of John.
People also called John “Mark.”
Many people had gathered at Mary’s house.
These people were praying.
passages.original: Συνιδών τε ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν τῆς Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐπικαλουμένου Μάρκου οὗ ἦσαν ἱκανοὶ συνηθροισμένοι καὶ προσευχόμενοι

passages.text: He knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
passages.sermon: Peter knocked at the outer gate.\r\nA servant girl came to answer the gate.\r\nHer name was Rhoda.
passages.original: κρούσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν θύραν τοῦ πυλῶνος προσῆλθεν παιδίσκη ὑπακοῦσαι ὀνόματι Ῥόδη

passages.text: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside and announced, “Peter is standing at the gate!”
passages.sermon:
Rhoda was a servant girl.  
She heard a man’s voice at the gate.  
She recognized the voice.  
The voice belonged to Peter.  
Rhoda felt great joy.  
She did not open the gate.  
She ran into the house.  
She told the people inside.  
She said, “Peter is standing at the gate.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ Πέτρου ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἤνοιξεν τὸν πυλῶνα εἰσδραμοῦσα δὲ ἀπήγγειλεν ἑστάναι τὸν Πέτρον πρὸ τοῦ πυλῶνος

passages.text: “You are out of your mind,” they told her. But when she kept insisting it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.”
passages.sermon:
A group of people spoke to Rhoda, the servant girl.
They said, “You are out of your mind.”
Rhoda kept insisting that Peter was at the gate.
The people replied, “It must be his angel.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπαν Μαίνῃ ἡ δὲ διϊσχυρίζετο οὕτως ἔχειν οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον Ὁ ἄγγελός ἐστιν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus.
Peter stood outside the gate.
Peter kept knocking on the door.
The people inside heard the knocking.
They opened the door.
They saw Peter standing there.
They were amazed.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐπέμενεν κρούων ἀνοίξαντες δὲ εἶδαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξέστησαν

passages.text: Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus.
Peter used his hand to signal for silence.
Peter spoke to the people.
Peter explained how the Lord brought him out of prison.
Peter said, “Tell James and the brothers about this.”
Peter left and went to another place.
passages.original: κατασείσας δὲ αὐτοῖς τῇ χειρὶ σιγᾶν διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ὁ Κύριος αὐτὸν ἐξήγαγεν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς εἶπέν τε Ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰακώβῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ταῦτα καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἕτερον τόπον

passages.text: At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.
passages.sermon:
The soldiers could not find Peter.
Daybreak came.
The soldiers became very disturbed.
They did not know what had happened to Peter.
There was great confusion among the soldiers.
passages.original: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἦν τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις τί ἄρα ὁ Πέτρος ἐγένετο

passages.text: After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the king.
Herod searched for Peter.
Herod did not find Peter.
Herod questioned the guards.
Herod ordered the guards to be executed.
Herod left Judea.
Herod went to Caesarea.
Herod stayed in Caesarea for some time.
passages.original: Ἡρῴδης δὲ ἐπιζητήσας αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ εὑρὼν ἀνακρίνας τοὺς φύλακας ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι καὶ κατελθὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς Καισάρειαν διέτριβεν

passages.text: Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king’s country for food.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the king.
Herod was very angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon.
The people of Tyre and Sidon came together to meet Herod.
They wanted to speak with him.
They persuaded Blastus to help them.
Blastus was in charge of the king’s bedroom.
With Blastus’s help, they asked Herod for peace.
They needed peace because their land received food from the king’s country.
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ θυμομαχῶν Τυρίοις καὶ Σιδωνίοις ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ παρῆσαν πρὸς αὐτόν καὶ πείσαντες Βλάστον τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος τοῦ βασιλέως ᾐτοῦντο εἰρήνην διὰ τὸ τρέφεσθαι αὐτῶν τὴν χώραν ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλικῆς

passages.text: On the appointed day, Herod donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the king.
On the appointed day, Herod put on his royal robes.
He sat on his throne.
He spoke to the people.
passages.original: τακτῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐνδυσάμενος ἐσθῆτα βασιλικὴν καὶ καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐδημηγόρει πρὸς αὐτούς

passages.text: And they began to shout, “This is the voice of a god, not a man!”
passages.sermon:
The people listened to Herod.
They shouted loudly.
They said, “This is the voice of a god.”
They said, “This is not the voice of a man.”
passages.original: ὁ δὲ δῆμος ἐπεφώνει Θεοῦ φωνὴ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: Immediately, because Herod did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.
passages.sermon:
Herod was a king.
Herod did not give glory to God.
An angel of the Lord struck Herod down immediately.
Worms ate Herod.
Herod died.
passages.original: Παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐπάταξεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἔδωκεν τὴν δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ γενόμενος σκωληκόβρωτος ἐξέψυξεν

passages.text: But the word of God continued to spread and multiply.
passages.sermon:
The word of God grew.
The word of God spread.
The word of God multiplied.
Many people heard the word of God.
Many people believed the word of God.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο

passages.text: When Barnabas and Saul had fulfilled their mission to Jerusalem, they returned, bringing with them John, also called Mark.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas and Saul were Christian leaders and missionaries.
They completed their mission in Jerusalem.
They returned from Jerusalem.
They brought John with them.
People also called John by the name Mark.
passages.original: Βαρνάβας δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν συμπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάννην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μάρκον
